claims.says: If the id space meets its contract and the type matrix is as wide as the type table, each relationship a successful delete reports loses its type entry, endpoints and tensor entry and is recycled.
Commit validation succeeds exactly when both id batches verify and every taken, non-recycled relationship id has endpoints at two live nodes.
The model of the Rust IdSpace mutators (create, release, cancel, open_batch, verify) satisfies the id-space contract that the graph theorems assume.
Growing a matrix capacity in positive chunks, starting from a capacity at most GrB_INDEX_MAX, never produces a capacity above GrB_INDEX_MAX.
If the label matrices and the node-label matrix agree and every label id exists, adding labels to nodes keeps them in agreement and records every requested node-label pair.
